account.note: FOUR LEVELS CHECKED, FOUR CLEAR, AND THE STOP MOVED FURTHER AWAY RATHER THAN CLOSER. OKLO is 44.84 bid against a 45.1499 average, so the position is -0.69%, 0.62 of unrealized loss on a 90.30 cost, against a 54.18 target that needs the bid up 20.8% and a 41.54 stop that needs it down 7.4%. The time stop is the 8/14 close, today session one of five. No option is held, so no no-fly window can apply, and the calendar was re-pulled live rather than carried forward - 934 earnings events across 8/10 to 8/14, OKLO in none of them, SMCI on 8/11 pm verified at an 0.88 estimate still the only watched name inside the window. Nothing was hit, so nothing is proposed. THE LAST HOUR'S WARNING DID NOT MATERIALISE, AND THAT IS RECORDED WITH THE SAME PROMINENCE IT WAS ISSUED. The 12:22 run wrote down that the 41.54 stop had closed to 6.2% on a name that had already travelled 8.57% that day, and that an ordinary continuation of the session reaches it. The session did not continue that way: the bid rose 0.57 to 44.84 and the stop is 7.4% away, wider than an hour ago and wider than at 11:22. The warning was worth writing and it was worth not acting on, which are two separate findings and this run owes both. Selling at -1.95% because -8% looked reachable would have been the error the note explicitly refused to make, and an hour later the distance had gone the other way. THE FINDING IS THAT LAST HOUR'S DIVERGENCE INVERTED. The 12:22 read was that the board had stopped falling while the position had not - breadth 9 red of 12, six names up and six down, OKLO alone at a new low - and it drew from that a name-specific problem, a name that had declined to participate in two of its own complex's bounces. Both halves reversed inside the hour. Breadth is 11 RED of 12, the worst read of the day, with SMCI the only green name; ten of the twelve names are bid lower than at 12:22; and OKLO is one of only two that are higher. The name that was singled out for falling alone is now rising nearly alone. THIS IS THE THIRD TELL TO INVERT INSIDE AN HOUR TODAY and the pattern is now the finding rather than any one of them: 10:22 offered SOUN and UPST as evidence and both inverted by 11:22; 11:22's own bounce read was given back; 12:22's divergence is reversed here. Three hours of intraday character-reading on a twelve-name board have produced three reversals, which is the argument for a slot that enforces levels and does not trade its own narrative. Deployable is 919.58 settled with nothing pending. NO NEW ORDER IN THE ACCOUNT SINCE THE 10:39 FILL, queried directly rather than inferred: one order exists in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET at 45.1499 on a 45.40 limit, placed_agent agentic, with no specification from any run here behind it. The escalation is carried a fourth hour unchanged and uncompounded. Against the 2026-08-10 concentration rule the book is one name of four, 8.9% of account value at the bid against a 40% single-name ceiling, and one of the two the nuclear complex allows.

account.operatorNote: OPERATOR, 2026-08-10, answering the funding escalation carried in the notes above rather than editing either of them. The 900.00 is a deposit I made; the account is funded to about 1000 and the cash is spendable. This answers the deposit and NOTHING ELSE - it is not an authorisation for the OKLO order the 10:46 sync found, which no run here published and which arrived through the same agentic channel escalated on 8/7; that escalation stands open and unanswered. Three rule changes go with it and all three are written up in docs/RULES.md with their arithmetic, because a licence recorded without its constraints is how this record stops being worth reading. The position ceiling goes from two to four, capped at 40% in any one name and at two names in any one complex - the complex cap is the one that matters on a board whose whole universe moves together. Overnight holds are not a change: they were always allowed, the five-session time stop stands, and it is not extendable by conviction. The objective is still about 10% a day, which is roughly 101 dollars at this size and needs a fully deployed four-name book to average +10% in a session against a +20% take-profit; where the objective and the rulebook conflict, the rulebook wins and the retro records the shortfall. What the deposit does NOT do is reopen options - that refusal has been on spread for three sessions, most recently 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling, and no balance narrows a spread. The 10:22 hourly was right to escalate this rather than size against it.
account.openingNote: THIS IS THE OPENING READ AND THE DAILY ENTRY MANDATE IS DISCHARGED, forced on item 1: buy 12 JOBY at a 8.85 limit, target 10.62, stop 8.14, time stop the 8/14 close, expiring 10:30 ET. Exits were checked before entries and there was nothing to check - a flat book means no target, no stop, no time stop and no option expiry no-fly window was due, and none went unenforced. Two things this run settled that were handed to it by name. FIRST, the straddle Friday's pre-close owed to this slot was pulled: the SMCI 8/14 32 call marks 2.51 against a 2.05 put, a 4.56 straddle on a 32.21 spot, so the market prices a 14.2% move on tomorrow night's print. SMCI is refused on that arithmetic and not on a view - the rulebook stops equity at -8%, and an 8% stop sits entirely inside a 14.2% expected move, so the realistic bad case gaps through the stop rather than filling at it and the exit written before entry would not be the exit taken. That matters beyond the refusal, because SMCI was the ONLY name on this board with a forward catalyst, and once it is gone item 1 cannot be passed anywhere on the list. SECOND, options were priced before any thesis was built, as the 8/5 rule requires, and are refused for a third consecutive session on SPREAD rather than affordability: eight contracts quoted live across JOBY, SOUN and SMR at 3-6 weeks, every one clearing the 0.40 delta floor, several affordable outright, and the tightest of them at 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling. Three different cash balances - 128.90, 126.06 and now 109.88 - have produced the same answer, which is the point at which it stops being about the balance. The tape reversed wholesale over the weekend: breadth is 10 RED of 12 after six consecutive 10-green reads on Friday, and the names that extended hardest into Friday's bell are the ones being unwound hardest now. JOBY is one of two green names and the only green one without a print tomorrow. That is the entry, and it is also exactly what is wrong with it - relative strength on a red tape is a real condition and it is not a catalyst, so item 1 is marked fail and the entry is published forced rather than dressed up as something cleaner.

positions.note: EVERY LEVEL CHECKED AGAINST THE 13:22 BID AND EVERY LEVEL CLEAR, which remains the only claim this slot is entitled to make. Target 54.18 needs the 44.84 bid up 20.8%; the 41.54 stop needs it down 7.4%; the position is -0.69% on the bid, 0.62 of unrealized loss on a 90.30 cost; the time stop is the 8/14 close with today session one of five. No-fly re-pulled live rather than carried: 934 earnings events across 8/10 to 8/14 with OKLO in none of them, and no option is held for the window to bite on in any case. THE STOP MOVED AWAY, NOT CLOSER, AND THE LAST RUN'S WARNING IS THEREFORE UNSPENT RATHER THAN VINDICATED. At 12:22 this row recorded that the stop had closed to 6.2% on a name that had already covered 8.57% of ground that day, and that an ordinary continuation of the session reaches it. The bid instead rose 0.57 and the stop is 7.4% away - further than an hour ago, further than at 11:22. Both halves of that note stand: writing the distance down in advance was right, and refusing to pre-empt the level at -1.95% was also right, because the hour that followed moved the other way. A stop that looks reachable is not a stop that has been reached, and this is the cleanest instance of that the record has yet produced. THE DIVERGENCE THAT DEFINED LAST HOUR HAS INVERTED. At 12:22 the board was firming while this name made a new low, and the reading offered was a name-specific problem in a name that had sat out two of its complex's bounces. This hour the board is 11 red of 12, the worst breadth of the day, ten of twelve names are bid below their 12:22 quotes, and OKLO is one of only two that are higher. It remains the worst name on the day at -7.39% for a fifth consecutive read, so the position's absolute standing is unchanged; what reversed is the relative story built on top of it. That story is retracted rather than quietly dropped, and the durable point is that three consecutive hours of character-reading on this board have each been contradicted by the next hour. Everything already said about the entry stands: this is the name the 10:22 candidate row refused under item 2 as day one of a decline, and the fill sits within a nickel of the bid at which it was refused. Provenance is unchanged and unresolved - one order in this account since 8/7, tagged to the agentic channel, no specification from any run here behind it, and nothing new in the hundred and sixty minutes since. That is the retro's to answer; this slot's job is to enforce the levels on a position that exists, whoever opened it, and the levels are clear. Tagged nuclear, which puts SMR and LEU on the same two-name limit as this position.

entryWatch.setup: JOBY post-earnings continuation - EXPIRED UNEXECUTED, and the fourth re-mark is the worst of the four
entryWatch.trigger: None, and the trigger stays dead in both directions. The 8.85 limit expired at 10:30 ET; JOBY is 8.63 bid, twenty-two cents BELOW the level, and re-striking a dead specification is a mid-session entry this slot refuses whether the name is above the limit or under it.
entryWatch.why: FOUR RE-MARKS, EACH ONE WORSE THAN THE LAST, AND NOT ONE OF THEM IS A RULE. At 10:22 this board recorded that the forced 8.85 entry would be showing a gain, JOBY being 9.05 bid and 2.3% past the limit. At 11:22 it was 8.78 and the specification would have been -0.79%. At 12:22, 8.67 and -2.03%. It is 8.63 bid now and that specification would be -2.49%. Every one of those statements was true when written, the sequence is monotone in one direction, and the reason it is tracked at all is that the forced arm is measured separately rather than blended into an average that would hide it. What the sequence demonstrates is the ground the 10:22 refusal actually rested on: a name that runs 2.3% past its level in forty minutes can come back through it and keep going for three more hours, so chasing it upward would have been the error rather than the missed opportunity it looked like at the time. JOBY has now given back the whole of the +4.7% it carried at 10:22 and is -0.12% on the day, having crossed from green to red this hour.

entryWatch.setup: SMCI pre-earnings - REFUSED on its own straddle, now the last full session before the print
entryWatch.trigger: None. The 8/14 32-strike straddle prices a 14.2% move on the 8/11 print and an 8% stop cannot survive it. Calendar re-confirmed live at 13:22 against 934 events in the 8/10-8/14 window: 8/11, pm, verified, estimate 0.88, and still the only watched name reporting inside it.
entryWatch.why: Unchanged in arithmetic and softer in tape - 31.83 bid, +2.25%, against +3.5% an hour ago and +5.7% at 10:22, so the give-back resumed after one flat hour. None of that touches the refusal, which was never about direction. The 8/14 32 call marked 2.51 against a 2.05 put for a 4.56 straddle on a 32.21 spot: a 14.2% implied move against a rulebook stop of 8%. An 8% stop sitting entirely inside a 14.2% expected move is an exit the event is priced to jump rather than fill, which is the sense in which item 3 is a gate and not a formality. Any 3-6 week option necessarily spans the print and is forbidden outright, so the option route was never reachable either. The print is now about twenty-seven hours out and this board holds nothing in it. Worth noting what the refusal is currently costing on paper and stating it anyway: SMCI is the only green name on a board that is 11 red of 12, which is exactly the shape of tape in which a pre-earnings bid looks like strength. It was refused at 09:41 on a number, and a number does not stop being the reason because the name held up for a session.

entryWatch.setup: The speculative complex - the stabilisation lasted exactly one hour
entryWatch.trigger: No level. Breadth deteriorated to 11 red of 12 from 9 red, the worst read of the day; RGTI's green flip lasted a single hour, and ten of the twelve names are bid lower than at 12:22 against six lower the hour before. One flat hour inside a three-hour decline was an interruption, not a base, which is what the last run said and is now the answer rather than the caution.
entryWatch.why: THE READ IS THAT THIS BOARD KEEPS INVERTING ITS OWN TELLS INSIDE AN HOUR, AND THAT IS NOW THE FINDING. Three consecutive hours have each produced a character-read that the next hour contradicted. 10:22 named SOUN and UPST as evidence of an unfinished give-back and both were higher an hour later. 11:22 recorded the bounce being given back and called the complex resumed-falling; 12:22 found it split evenly and firming. 12:22 then read a divergence - board stabilising, OKLO alone at a new low, a name-specific problem - and this hour the board is at its worst breadth of the day while OKLO is one of only two names higher. Each read was defensible on the numbers in front of it and each was overturned by the next set. The conclusion is not that any one of them was careless; it is that hour-scale narrative on a twelve-name correlated board has a demonstrated hit rate near chance, and the slot that keeps writing them is also the slot with no entry authority, which is fortunate. Nothing here is buyable and nothing is proposed: this slot opens nothing, the bar for a mid-session entry is higher than the open's by design, and the last hour of a three-hour decline that briefly paused is not a day-2/3 pullback. The two nuclear names outside the position are LEU at -0.57% and SMR at -5.80%, and the complex cap would allow exactly one of them.
